THE SCHOOL HALL · CHRISTMAS · AGES 2–5

Christmas — what it is and how little kids celebrate.

Christmas is the December holiday of lights and songs: trees, presents, carols and a family table on December 25.

Back to the Hall ↗
WHAT IS CHRISTMAS?

What’s this? Why do we celebrate it?

Christmas comes every year on December 25. Many families celebrate it as the birthday of Jesus, and nearly everyone who celebrates — religious or not — shares the same cozy picture: a tree with lights, songs on the radio, special food, presents, and people who love each other gathering under one roof. The deeper idea underneath the wrapping paper is giving: we give presents because we are glad the people we love are here.

For a little kid, Christmas is a season of tiny traditions that repeat every year — the same song, the same cookies, the same star on top of the tree — and that repetition is exactly what makes it feel like magic.

TRY IT · ACTIVITIES FOR KIDS

December, kid-sized.

Count the lights on the tree — start at ten and let your child keep going as high as they can. Sing one carol every bath time until it sticks. Make paper ornaments for the lower branches (the branches a two-year-old can actually reach). Wrap a present in scribbled paper for a grandparent. Stir the cookie dough and shake the sprinkles. And on a quiet evening, retell the night before with the Sequence Stories card in your hand: first we hang it, then we light it, then we sing.
